note.label: Psalm 149: The High Praises and a Two-Edged Sword

precepts.why:
“Let Israel rejoice in him that made him: let the children of Zion be joyful in their King.” Solomon assembled the elders of Israel to bring up the ark of the covenant “out of the city of David, which is Zion.” Zion is another word for Jerusalem or Israel. Jerusalem or Israel was a people before it was a place, so when scripture refers to Zion it points to the children of Israel.

The King the children of Zion are joyful in is the same horn of his people, the horn of salvation, which is Christ. He will beautify the meek with salvation; meek means submissive or obedient, so if you keep the commandments and are obedient to the Most High you will have salvation. Then come the high praises in the mouth and a twoedged sword in the hand: the honour the saints, the children of Israel, receive when they overcome these people is the privilege of binding their kings with chains and their nobles with fetters of iron. If you do not understand that we are Israelites, you will read this and think it is talking about a time during David or during the kings, but it is talking about the future.

precepts.why:
“The meek also shall increase their joy in the Lord, and the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.” Who are the meek? “Let Israel rejoice in him that made him: let the children of Zion be joyful in their King.” “For the Lord taketh pleasure in his people: he will beautify the meek with salvation.” The meek is Israel, the people the Most High takes pleasure in and will beautify with salvation.

So all of it is about Israel. The deaf that “hear the words of the book” are Israel, in a spiritual deep sleep now beginning to wake and hear the word of God rightly. The blind whose eyes “shall see out of obscurity” are Israel, coming out of an obscurity like thinking Esau is white when he is red. And the meek who increase their joy in the Most High are Israel, rejoicing in him that made them.

points: “For the Lord taketh pleasure in his people”: on the street, you want to stress that. He don’t take pleasure in everybody on the planet; he takes pleasure in his people. “He will beautify the meek with salvation”: he’s going to beautify us once again.

note.label: The Song Of Moses & The Song Of The Lamb

points: “Let the saints be joyful in glory: let them sing aloud upon their beds”, because we’re going to be in righteousness in the kingdom of heaven.

note.label: The Song Of Moses & The Song Of The Lamb

points: “Let the high praises of God be in their mouth, and a twoedged sword in their hand”: see the picture; this is what the Bible is talking about. The word of God in our mouth is the Bible.

note.label: The Song Of Moses & The Song Of The Lamb

points: What are we going to do? “To execute vengeance upon the heathen”: we’re going to execute vengeance upon the nations, “and punishments upon the people”: upon all the peoples of the earth.

note.label: The Song Of Moses & The Song Of The Lamb

points: “To bind their kings with chains, and their nobles with fetters of iron”: we’re going to bind their kings in chains. Just like they did to us, we’re going to do to them.

note.label: The Song Of Moses & The Song Of The Lamb

points: “To execute upon them the judgment written”: whatever this Bible says, we’re going to execute it upon them. “This honour have all his saints. Praise ye the Lord.”
